title: Dirt Bike Insurance Coverage: What It Pays, What It Excludes & Insurance for Motocross Bikes
description: Dirt bike insurance coverage explained: liability, theft, collision and medical options, why homeowners won't pay, and how motocross bike insurance works.
author: Insurance Bhaiya Research Desk
keyTakeaways: Dirt bike insurance is a specialty off-road motorcycle policy. Liability, comprehensive (theft, fire, vandalism), collision and medical payments are each chosen separately.
Homeowners insurance usually excludes motorized vehicles away from your premises, so it's often useless for a dirt bike at the trail or on a friend's land.
Standard dirt bike policies exclude organized racing and timed events. Insurance for motocross bikes on the track usually requires event or track cover.

Whether you legally need it depends on where you ride. Most states don't require it on private land, but some do on public land or once the bike is registered. See [do dirt bikes need insurance](/qa/do-dirt-bikes-need-insurance/).
Dual-sport bikes plated for the street need a regular [motorcycle insurance](/learn/motorcycle-dirt-bike-powersport-insurance/) policy that meets state liability minimums.

faqs.question: Does dirt bike insurance cover theft?
faqs.answer: Only if you add comprehensive coverage. Liability-only dirt bike policies pay nothing for a stolen bike. Theft payouts are usually actual cash value minus your deductible, the same way as in [does motorcycle insurance cover theft](/qa/does-motorcycle-insurance-cover-theft/).

faqs.question: Is there insurance for motocross bikes used for racing?
faqs.answer: Yes, but not usually on a standard recreational policy, which excludes organized racing. Racers rely on track or event liability, sanctioning-body accident cover and off-season comprehensive on their own policy.

faqs.question: Do you need insurance for a dirt bike?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state and where you ride. Most states don't require it on private property, while some require it on public land or once the bike is registered. The state-by-state answer is in [do dirt bikes need insurance](/qa/do-dirt-bikes-need-insurance/).

faqs.question: Will my homeowners insurance cover my kid's dirt bike?
faqs.answer: Often not, especially away from home. Most homeowners policies exclude motorized vehicles off the insured premises and exclude the vehicle itself as property. Ask about a recreational-vehicle endorsement or buy a separate off-road policy.

content.text: A new 250cc or 450cc motocross bike can cost more than a used car, and it spends its life being jumped, crashed and loaded onto trailers. It also typically sits in an unlocked garage or pickup bed, which makes it an easy target for thieves. Yet most [riders](/learn/what-is-an-insurance-rider/) ride uninsured, because they assume their homeowners policy covers it or that no one requires insurance. This guide explains exactly what **dirt bike insurance coverage** pays, where it stops, and what changes when you race. It's one spoke in our [Motorcycle, Dirt Bike & Powersport Insurance hub](/learn/motorcycle-dirt-bike-powersport-insurance/).
What Dirt Bike Insurance Coverage Includes

rows: Injuries to other riders or bystanders and damage to their property when you're at fault
Anyone riding on shared trails, public land or others' property
Theft, fire, vandalism, flood, falling objects, and damage while trailered or stored
Owners of bikes worth more than a few thousand dollars. This is the same coverage that answers [does motorcycle insurance cover theft](/qa/does-motorcycle-insurance-cover-theft/)
Damage to your bike from crashes, drops and hitting obstacles, minus the [deductible](/glossary/deductible/)
Newer or financed bikes. Often skipped on older bikes
Medical costs for you or a guest rider regardless of fault, up to a small limit
Families whose kids and friends ride the same bike
Injuries to a guest rider you let use the bike
Owners who lend bikes (a leading cause of off-road lawsuits)
Aftermarket suspension, exhaust, graphics and riding gear
Damage to or theft of the bike trailer
Riders who tow to trails and tracks

content.title: Uninsured Motorist Usually Isn't Included Off-Road
content.text: Uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage is designed for road crashes. Pure off-road policies often leave it out or limit it, which is another reason to keep strong health coverage. Compare your plan's exposure with the [health insurance calculator](/health-insurance-calculator/).
Why Your Homeowners Policy Probably Won't Cover the Dirt Bike

Standard homeowners forms contain a motorized-vehicle [exclusion](/glossary/exclusion/). It generally removes liability coverage for motorized land vehicles used away from the 'insured location'. It also removes property coverage for the vehicles themselves, apart from narrow exceptions such as small garden equipment. In practice:

items: **The bike is stolen from your garage:** Often excluded under property coverage, because motorized vehicles are carved out. You need comprehensive on a dirt bike policy.

**Your child's friend crashes on your backyard track:** Coverage depends on your policy wording. Some forms give limited on-premises liability and many don't. Check the language using [how to read an insurance policy](/learn/how-to-read-an-insurance-policy/).
**You injure a hiker on a public trail:** Almost always excluded under homeowners. Only an off-road liability policy responds.

**Adding an endorsement:** Some insurers sell a recreational-vehicle endorsement that extends homeowners liability. See [what is an insurance endorsement](/learn/what-is-an-insurance-endorsement/) and compare its price with a standalone policy.

content.text: Insurance for Motocross Bikes: What Changes When You Race

Almost every recreational dirt bike policy excludes 'racing, speed contests, or organized competitive events'. That covers practice laps at a sanctioned track on race day, timed enduros and scored events. Motocross racers usually piece together cover from three sources:

items: **Track or event liability**, carried by the promoter or track. It protects the track, and riders sign waivers. Your personal exposure may remain. See [event liability insurance](/learn/event-liability-insurance/) for how organizers structure it.
**Rider accident / medical cover**, often offered through sanctioning-body memberships. It pays limited medical costs after a racing injury.
**Off-season comprehensive** on your own dirt bike policy, which protects the bike against theft and fire while stored or trailered, when no racing exclusion applies.

content.title: Read the Racing Exclusion Before Race Day
content.text: If you crash at a practice day that the insurer treats as 'organized competition', your collision claim can be denied outright. Ask your insurer in writing whether open-practice days, trail rides with timing and club events are covered.
How Much Does Dirt Bike Insurance Cost?

Because off-road bikes spend no time in traffic, liability-only dirt bike insurance usually costs less than street motorcycle insurance. Many riders pay low hundreds of dollars a year or less. Adding comprehensive and collision on a new race bike raises the price with the bike's value. The main rating factors are bike value, engine size, the rider's age, where the bike is stored, and deductible choice. Model your deductible with the [deductible vs premium calculator](/deductible-calculator/). For comparison, see street-bike costs in [Colorado](/qa/how-much-is-motorcycle-insurance-in-colorado/) and [Ohio](/qa/how-much-is-motorcycle-insurance-in-ohio/).
Dirt Bike vs Dual-Sport vs ATV: Which Policy Do You Need?

rows: Usually no. Some states require it on public land. See [what states require dirt bike insurance](/qa/do-dirt-bikes-need-insurance/)
In some states. See [quad bike & ATV insurance](/learn/quad-bike-atv-insurance/)

content.text: Before You Buy: 5-Point Dirt Bike Coverage Checklist

items: Confirm where you'll ride (private land, public trails, OHV parks or tracks) and check the state rules in [do dirt bikes need insurance](/qa/do-dirt-bikes-need-insurance/).
Ask your homeowners insurer in writing whether the bike is covered on and off premises.
Choose liability limits that protect your savings. Lending the bike to friends is where most lawsuits start.
Add comprehensive if the bike is worth more than you'd happily lose. Theft and trailer fires are common.
Get the racing exclusion wording in writing before any track day, and run a final check with the [policy review checklist](/policy-review-checklist/).
